summary: The candidate is false as stated because it applies Brunn--Minkowski to endpoint intersections that are allowed to be empty. In particular, (9) fails when P is empty. The calibrated specialization avoids this specific defect because p,q>0, but those positivity assumptions are absent from the general statement.
critical_errors: The proof applies planar Brunn--Minkowski to P and A_2 without establishing that P is nonempty, even though the statement explicitly permits empty cells. Take A_0=A_2=K to be the unit disk, f_i(x_1,x_2)=x_2, f_j(x_1,x_2)=x_1+2, f_ell(x_1,x_2)=-x_1-x_2-3, a_i=2, and any a_ell. Then the affine functions are nonconstant and sum to -1, (A_0+A_2)/2=K, P is empty, c_j=0, and r=pi. Hence U,E,rho are all empty or zero, while (9) asserts 0 >= pi/4.
gaps: The same nonemptiness problem occurs in (25)-(26): either endpoint halfspace intersection defining G_ell or G_i may be empty under the stated hypotheses, in which case Brunn--Minkowski does not give the displayed positive area term from its empty Minkowski sum. The sentence invoking Alternative 1 and p,q>0 relies on assumptions that are not part of the candidate statement.
repair_hints: Require P to be nonempty before (9), and require both endpoint halfspace intersections in each of (10) and (11) to be nonempty before (25)-(26). The simpler sufficient assumptions p>0 and q>0 cover all of these requirements. Alternatively, restrict the assertions explicitly to the calibrated regime, where p,q>0.
